# Surfaces

From [the component index](../components.md). A prop with `?` is optional, and `= x` is its default. An indented line is the shape of a value the prop takes. In the examples, `children`, `transactions`, the icons and the handlers stand for the screen's own content, data and state.

## Card, CardHeader, CardTitle, CardDescription, CardContent, CardFooter

```tsx
import { Card } from "@tuja/ui/components/card";
import { CardHeader } from "@tuja/ui/components/card-header";
import { CardTitle } from "@tuja/ui/components/card-title";
import { CardDescription } from "@tuja/ui/components/card-description";
import { CardContent } from "@tuja/ui/components/card-content";
import { CardFooter } from "@tuja/ui/components/card-footer";
```

A bordered surface that groups one topic. `Card` is already a `stack.item`, so put content straight in it.

### Card

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — Card contents.
- `interactive?: boolean = false` — Adds hover, focus and press affordances for a card that acts as a clickable control.
- `intent?: "danger"` — Draws the edge in the colour of an Intent and leaves the rest of the card as it is.

### CardHeader

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — Header content — typically a `CardTitle` and a `CardDescription`.
- `action?: ReactNode` — Control at the header's trailing edge — a menu button, dismiss, or badge.

### CardTitle

Props (also `css`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The card's title.
- `level?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3` — Heading rank. Defaults to `3`; set it to keep the document outline honest when the card sits under a deeper or shallower heading.
- `id?: string` — Id applied to the rendered heading — the other half of the named-region pattern, where the `Card` carries `aria-labelledby` pointing here.
- `ref?: Ref<HTMLHeadingElement>` — Ref to the rendered heading element.

### CardDescription

Props (also `css`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The supporting copy.
- `id?: string` — Id applied to the rendered paragraph, e.g. for an `aria-describedby` on the control the card is about.
- `ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>` — Ref to the rendered paragraph.

### CardContent

Props: `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`.

### CardFooter

Props: `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`.

Example:

```tsx
function CardExample() {
  return (
    <Card>
      <CardHeader action={<Badge size="sm">Beta</Badge>}>
        <CardTitle level={2}>Morning report</CardTitle>
        <CardDescription>One summary of the last day’s mail.</CardDescription>
      </CardHeader>
      <Text look="bodySmall">{children}</Text>
    </Card>
  );
}
```

## Section

```tsx
import { Section } from "@tuja/ui/components/section";
```

A labelled block with a heading row and optional actions, with no surface of its own: a quiet label by default, a real heading with `look="heading"`, such as the day of a timeline.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<section>`):

- `children?: ReactNode` — Section body. Leave it out when the description says all there is.
- `title: ReactNode` — The block's label. Rendered as a real heading, so keep it to a phrase.
- `description?: ReactNode` — A muted line under the label that says what the block holds.
- `icon?: ReactNode` — Decorative icon before the label, rendered `aria-hidden`.
- `actions?: ReactNode` — Controls parked at the end of the heading row — a "see all" link, a filter.
- `level?: 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 = 3` — Heading rank for the label.
- `look?: "label" | "heading" = "label"` — How the title reads.
- `divider?: boolean` — Rules the section off from what precedes it.

Example:

```tsx
function SectionExample() {
  return (
    <Section
      level={2}
      title="Recently done"
      actions={
        <Button href="/todos/done" look="ghost" size="sm">
          See all
        </Button>
      }
    >
      {children}
    </Section>
  );
}
```

## Disclosure

```tsx
import { Disclosure } from "@tuja/ui/components/disclosure";
```

A row that opens a panel under it, such as advanced options or an FAQ.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — Panel content, revealed when open.
- `summary: ReactNode` — Header content — the whole row is the trigger, so keep this text and decoration only.
- `icon?: ReactNode` — Decorative leading icon in the header, rendered `aria-hidden`.
- `trailing?: ReactNode` — Content between the summary and the caret — a count, a status badge.
- `indicator?: ReactNode` — The open/closed indicator. Defaults to a caret that rotates on open; pass a node to swap it, or `null` to drop it.
- `look?: "plain" | "card" | "inline" = "plain"` — `"plain"` (the default) is chrome-free, for a disclosure that sits inside a surface something else already owns.
- `open?: boolean` — Controlled open state. Omit to let the component own it.
- `onOpenChange?: (open: boolean) => void` — Called with the next state whenever the trigger toggles.
- `defaultOpen?: boolean = false` — Initial open state when uncontrolled.

Example:

```tsx
function DisclosureExample() {
  return (
    <Disclosure look="card" summary="Lost your passkey?">
      <Text look="bodySmall">Ask another member for a recovery link.</Text>
    </Disclosure>
  );
}
```

## Divider

```tsx
import { Divider } from "@tuja/ui/components/divider";
```

A line between two blocks that are not in a list.

Props (also `css`):

- `orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical" = "horizontal"` — Line direction. Renders a semantic `<hr>` when horizontal, or a `role="separator"` `<div>` when vertical.
- `look?: "subtle" | "bold" | "decorative" = "subtle"` — Weight / treatment of the rule.
- `ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>` — Ref to the rendered element (`<hr>` when horizontal, `<div>` when vertical).

## ScrollMask

```tsx
import { ScrollMask } from "@tuja/ui/components/scroll-mask";
```

A scroll region whose content blurs out at each edge it can still scroll to.

Props (also `css`, and every attribute of `<div>`):

- `children: ReactNode` — The region's content. It renders inside the scroller, which owns the overflow and moves under the bands.
- `orientation?: "horizontal" | "vertical" = "vertical"` — Scroll axis. `"vertical"` masks the block-start and block-end edges; `"horizontal"` masks the inline-start and inline-end edges.
- `radius?: number = 8` — Nominal blur radius in px against the edge, where the mask is strongest — the stacked layers compound to slightly above it.
- `depth?: string = "1.5rem"` — How far the mask reaches from the edge into the region, as any CSS length — past the chrome's inner edge instead, on an edge with a chrome slot.
- `startChrome?: ReactNode` — Chrome pinned over the region's start edge — a header row the content scrolls beneath.
- `startMask?: boolean = true` — Blurs the start edge while the region can scroll back to it.
- `endChrome?: ReactNode` — Chrome pinned over the region's end edge — a pinned footer or action bar.
- `endChromeCss?: StyleProp` — StyleX styles merged over the `endChrome` slot's own, which pin it sticky against the end edge — for chrome that sits somewhere else, such as a footer fixed to the viewport.
- `scrollButtons?: { startLabel: string; endLabel: string }` — A button per edge that scrolls the region one page towards that edge, and the accessible name for each — the package ships no i18n, so the names come in as props.
- `clipMargin?: string` — How far the scroller's overflow clip reaches past the root, on the axis that does not scroll, as any CSS length — room for content that grows on hover or on focus, or that casts a shadow, so it paints out over the neighbours instead of being cut at the edge.
- `contentCss?: StyleProp` — StyleX styles merged over the SCROLLER's own — padding, the layout of the children, scroll manners, scrollbar treatment, and the focus ring.

## FlowBlock

```tsx
import { FlowBlock } from "@tuja/ui/components/flow-block";
```

Wrap content that sits under a `Disclosure` and is not already a block, so it moves when the panel opens.

Props (also `css`):

- `surface?: boolean = false` — The element paints a surface, and a `Disclosure` can be in it: during the motion, the lower edge of the surface moves with the panel.
- `as?: "div" | "section" | "li" | "hr" | "nav" = "div"` — The element to render.
- `ref?: Ref<HTMLElement>` — Ref to the rendered element.
